samples.summary: New text inverts the actual default of the only server-side write gate (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`), and contradicts the same file 18 lines later
samples.evidence:
This change adds, in the security design doc for sharing: "What stops a write is the Yorkie auth webhook — see **Server-side write enforcement, once enabled** below, and note that it is off in a stock deployment." (sharing.md:293-296). The same change adds the matching claim in code: `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:1062-1066` — "per-document write authority is enforced server-side by the Yorkie auth webhook, which a deployment must switch out of its default shadow mode (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`) for a downgrade or a revocation to actually stop a write."

Both are false. `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29-31` is `return raw?.trim().toLowerCase() !== 'false';` — i.e. unset/absent = ENFORCE, and only the literal string `false` selects shadow mode. Its own header says "**Enforcing is the default.**" `packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:120-137` says the same, as does the *unchanged* section of the very file the new text was added to: `docs/design/sharing.md:314` — "**Enforcing is the default**: registering the methods on the Yorkie project is the whole switch, and `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` needs no value". `packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:185` and `packages/frontend/README.md:39` agree. Backed by a test: `packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.spec.ts:410` — 'enforces when YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE is unset'.

Attack/impact chain: this is the document an operator or the next developer reads to decide the deployment's write-authorization posture for anonymous share visitors. Being told enforcement is "off in a stock deployment" and that one "must switch out of its default shadow mode" invites exactly the wrong remediation — an operator debugging a viewer-side denial, or one trying to make the documented default explicit, sets `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false`, which is the one value that disables the only place a share-link `viewer`'s write is refused (`hasAccess`: `needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`, yorkie-auth.controller.ts:370). The enforcement module's own comment explains the design intent this text undoes: "A typo enforces rather than silently opening the door." It also mis-scopes the threat model for future reviewers of this very feature, who will under-weight the client-side gates this PR is built on. Note two pre-existing copies of the same wrong claim already exist out of diff (`packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40`, `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4629`); this change propagates rather than corrects them, and puts one in the top-level design doc where it self-contradicts.

samples.summary: `revocableDocStore` revokes property *lookups*, not values already extracted — a raw `.doc` (the Yorkie CRDT handle) or a bound mutator captured before `dispose()` still writes afterwards
samples.evidence: While not revoked, the new proxy's `get` trap forwards non-function members verbatim (`if (typeof raw !== 'function') return raw;`, read-only.ts:199) and hands back a function bound to the *real* store (line 202), memoized. Revocation only changes what a *subsequent* property read returns. So any holder that extracted a member before `dispose()` keeps it: `const d = editor.getStore().doc` yields `YorkieDocStore`'s raw Yorkie `Document`, whose `update()` is the documented write path, and `const f = editor.getStore().insertText` yields a live bound mutator — both keep working after `disposed` flips. `readOnlyDocStore` deliberately hides data properties for precisely this reason and says so at read-only.ts:90-96 ("`YorkieDocStore.doc` is the CRDT handle, whose `update()` is the documented write path. Forwarding those would have left a wider hole"); the revocable wrapper cannot hide them while live without breaking transparency, so the hole is inherent to the approach rather than an oversight — but the claim it supports is stated unconditionally. `docs/design/sharing.md:290-291` asserts "so a stale handle cannot write through the rebuild", and `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3382-3386` asserts the accessors' copies "stop writing at `dispose()`". Both are true only of holders that kept the *handle object*; they are false for a holder that kept a member of it. I found no in-repo caller that extracts a member (`docs-find-bar.tsx:66-67` keeps the `Doc` and re-reads `getStore()` lazily; `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:496-499` reads `store.fonts` fresh each call), so this is currently unreachable in-tree — hence minor. Impact is bounded further because the design doc and `yorkie-auth.controller.ts` both place the real write boundary at the auth webhook. Suggest narrowing the claim, or refusing data-property forwarding for the known-sensitive keys.

samples.summary: Narrowing the fatal set to {404,410} means a 401/403 answer never evicts a live share session, so the client-side revocation bound can be defeated indefinitely
samples.evidence: `SHARE_LINK_VERDICT_STATUSES = new Set([404, 410])` (share-links.ts:152-155) replaces the previous "any 4xx except 408/429" rule, and `isShareLinkResolveFatal` (line 203) only evicts a live session on a member of that set. Everything else — including 401 and 403 — keeps the last good `resolved` forever while the interval retries, so the mounted view keeps presenting whatever role it opened with (`readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'`, shared-document.tsx:198/716). The stated justification is that `POST /share-links/resolve` only answers 404/410, which is true today (`ShareLinkService.findByToken` throws only `NotFoundException`/`GoneException`, share-link.service.ts:108-114). The weakness is that the client now depends on that invariant holding forever for an endpoint it does not control: if a deployment fronts the API with an auth proxy that 403s an anonymous POST, or a future handler adds a `ForbiddenException` (e.g. a per-document share kill-switch), the client silently stops honouring it and the only client-side bound on a revoked/downgraded link — the property this whole PR adds — disappears. The reverse direction was the bug being fixed, so the narrowing is defensible; the residual is that there is no telemetry or fail-safe for a persistently-erroring resolve (e.g. eviction after N consecutive failures spanning >M minutes), which would bound both directions.

samples.summary: The token-in-path `GET /share-links/:token/resolve` is retained, unauthenticated and with no deprecation gate, so the credential-in-URL exposure this change exists to remove stays reachable
samples.evidence: `@Get('share-links/:token/resolve')` (share-link.controller.ts:91) stays public and unchanged, justified as "for the one-shot callers that already exist (an older frontend served during a rollout)" (lines 80-82) and documented as retained in `docs/design/sharing.md:59-63`. No caller in the repo uses it any more — `packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.ts:110` is the only resolve client and now POSTs, and `packages/frontend/src/api/url.test.ts:167-176` was rewritten to assert the token never appears in the URL. So the route exists solely for cached bundles, with nothing recording when that window closes: no deprecation header, no counter, no removal ticket referenced. Any client still on the old bundle, or anyone who bookmarks/curls the old shape, keeps writing a live access-granting token into every intervening proxy, CDN and access log — the exact exposure the diff's own rationale describes (`logSafeUrl` redacts only this server's line, per SECRET_PATH_SEGMENTS, log-safe-url.ts:92). Recommend adding a removal trigger (a counter on the GET handler, or a dated removal note) so the legacy surface does not become permanent.

samples.summary: `refetchOnWindowFocus: true` with `staleTime: 0` plus a 60 s interval can exhaust the caller's own shared 120 req/min throttle bucket, and a 429 is deliberately non-fatal and retried
samples.evidence: The new query sets `refetchInterval: 60_000`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: true`, `staleTime: 0` (shared-document.tsx:1087-1089). With `staleTime: 0` every window-focus event issues a fresh unauthenticated resolve, so ordinary alt-tabbing produces one request per focus, unbounded, on top of the per-minute interval. The backend throttler is a single global bucket of 120 requests / 60 s keyed per IP (`ThrottlerModule.forRoot({ throttlers: [{ name: 'default', ttl: 60_000, limit: 120 }] })`, app.module.ts:97-104) shared with every other route, and `BACKEND_TRUST_PROXY` defaults to 0 (main.ts:39), so behind a NAT or corporate egress all viewers of a shared document collapse onto one bucket. Exhausting it 429s the *other* calls the same session needs (image fetches via `?token=`, `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share`), degrading the shared view. `shouldRetryShareLinkResolve` (share-links.ts:176) then retries a 429 once, adding a request to a bucket that is already full. Not a remote-attacker DoS — a visitor can only exhaust their own IP's budget — hence minor; a non-zero `staleTime` (e.g. half the interval) would remove the focus-storm without weakening the revocation bound.

samples.summary: Switching resolve from GET to POST promotes it from `debug` to `info` in the access log, so every anonymous share viewer now leaves a per-minute IP + user-agent heartbeat
samples.evidence: `customLogLevel` in app.module.ts:51-63 classifies any non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS request as a mutation and returns `'info'`; GETs return `'debug'`, which is silent at the default `LOG_LEVEL ?? 'info'` (line 34). `@Post('share-links/resolve')` (share-link.controller.ts:84) is therefore logged at info on *success*, once per `SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS` (60 s) per open tab, and the request serializer records `remoteAddress` and `user-agent` (app.module.ts:69-75). Before this change the resolve was a silent GET fired once per page load. The token itself is safe — pino logs no body, and the new path carries no secret — so this is not credential exposure; it is a new per-minute presence/IP trail for every anonymous share-link visitor for as long as the tab stays open, plus the log-volume that goes with it. Worth a deliberate decision (an `ignore` entry alongside `/health`, or an explicit note) rather than an accident of the GET→POST switch.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The claimed text exists verbatim at docs/design/sharing.md:293-296 ("note that it is off in a stock deployment") and packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:1062-1066 ("must switch out of its default shadow mode (YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true)"). Both invert the implementation: packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29-31 returns `raw?.trim().toLowerCase() !== 'false'`, so unset means ENFORCE and only the literal 'false' selects shadow mode; its own header (lines 5-12, 23-27) and packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:120-137 both state "Enforcing is the default". The same sharing.md contradicts itself 18 lines later at 314-321 and again at 347-348, and self-hosting.md:185 / frontend README.md:40 agree with the code. Not out of scope for the security lens: this is the design doc governing the posture of the only server-side write gate for anonymous share-link viewers (hasAccess: needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true), and the text steers an operator toward setting YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false — the one value that disables that gate — while under-weighting the client-side gates for future reviewers. No guard or caller neutralizes it. Major weakness, not refutable.
